tb21_profile.skill: Extract a date from a filename, build five overlapping windows relative to a fixed reference date (today, inclusive last-7, inclusive last-30, month-to-date, all-time) without off-by-one errors, tally three exact severity tokens per window, and emit a CSV whose rows and order are dictated exactly.
tb21_profile.domain: Log analysis and reporting: date arithmetic (datetime/timedelta or GNU date), filename parsing, severity counting, CSV output; Python or shell.
tb21_profile.task_form: Implement-from-spec: a deterministic aggregation pipeline with a rigidly specified output file.

searches: tools.py search all 'ERROR.{0,12}WARN|severity|WARN(ING)?, ?INFO|log level|last (7|30|24) (days|hours)|rolling window|date range' -n 40
tools.py search tmax 'YYYY-MM-DD.*\.log|filename.*date|date.*from the file ?name|last (7|30) days|month.to.date|rolling (7|30)|per.day count|daily (count|aggregat)|summary\.csv|period,severity' -n 28
tools.py search tmax '\bINFO\b.{0,40}\bWARN|\bWARN.{0,40}\bERROR\b|count(s)? of each (severity|level)|per.severity|group(ed)? by (level|severity)|log level.*count' -n 24
tools.py search all 'reference date|current date is|relative to (the|a) (current|reference|latest)|as of (the )?date|date -d|timedelta|dateutil|inclusive of|cutoff date|within the last' -n 30
tools.py search tmax 'older than|retention (policy|period)|N days|days ago|within (the )?(last|past)|date filter|between two dates|gap.fill|missing (days|dates)|calendar' -n 24
tools.py search rebench 'resample|date_range|month.end|start of the month|off.by.one.*(day|date)|inclusive|crontab|rotation|log file|date boundary|week' -n 26

TMax-15K.reason: Counting INFO/WARN/ERROR per level, with the exact failure mode of miscounting when a level word appears inside a message body. Same counting precision.
Logs named app_<YYYY-MM-DD>.log with LEVEL: INFO|WARNING|CRITICAL records; parse the date from the filename and filter by level.
Bucket log lines by time, emit zero for empty buckets, write summary.csv with an exact header and a specified sort. Same exact-CSV aggregation.
Daily event counts across a whole calendar month into a Date,Count CSV, gap-filling days with no events. Calendar-window aggregation.
Accept only LEVEL exactly INFO/WARN/ERROR (skip DEBUG/TRACE), bucket by hour, aggregate. Same exact-token filter plus time bucketing.
Aggregate counts across every log file in a directory, counting only lines with one status value, into a summary file with an exact schema.
Parse timestamps, index by time, and resample log-level counts into fixed windows; the pandas route to the same windowed tallies.
Parse two differently-formatted log files into a common LEVEL/timestamp shape, then deduplicate and aggregate. Same normalise-then-count pipeline.
Walk many .log files in a directory and aggregate per hour to find when issues started; multi-file log aggregation by time bucket.
Parse a log CSV whose level is INFO/WARNING/ERROR and whose messages span lines; correct record boundaries before counting.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Window is 'starting 30 days before the most recent commit up to that commit (inclusive)' - the inclusive relative-window arithmetic this task lives or dies on.
Identify the 30-day window ending at a reference commit and compute per-day counts across it. Reference-date window plus daily tallies.
Asks for the 30 days leading up to the latest commit but per-day counts over a 31-day period; forces explicit reasoning about window endpoints.
Past 30 days relative to the most recent commit, counting occurrences per day for one file. Same relative-window daily histogram.
Last 30 days relative to the latest commit, daily counts plus a within-window extremum. Relative-window filtering over dated records.
Normalise a date to ISO 8601 and compute complete elapsed years; date normalisation plus whole-period arithmetic against the current date.
Daily dated records into a report with overall totals and per-date subtotals; the same group-by-date-then-total shape, different output format.
Count how many times each event_type appears, emit counts as JSON plus a summary table, and reconcile against expected values.
Validate dated records, convert to TSV, aggregate per date. Category-by-date aggregation with a strict output format.
Count occurrences of each event_type in a dataset and write counts.json. Categorical tallying only, no date logic.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Count commits per day over the past 30 days, 'from 30 days ago through today, one day at a time' - the inclusive window plus per-day tally, in a shell task.
Compute complete elapsed years from a fixed birth date to the current date; whole-period date arithmetic with an exact single-value output.
Count occurrences of each event_type across a dataset and write the tallies to a structured file. Categorical counting with an exact output.
Extract the year and one value from each valid line and emit a two-field CSV with no extras; parse-then-exact-CSV with strict line filtering.
Recursively enumerate every log file under a logs tree and write sorted absolute paths; the file-discovery step of this task.
Reshape one CSV into another with an exactly specified row and column layout. Pure exact-CSV-output discipline.
Emit log records at debug/info/notice/warn/error/critical in order with a fixed format; the severity taxonomy, from the producing side.
Count records in two differently-formatted files and write both counts to one result file. Counting plus a fixed report.
Convert an NTP timestamp into a datetime rendered in an exact format; timestamp handling with a strict textual output.
Parse a CSV header with an unusual delimiter and emit an exactly specified string. Parsing edge case plus exact output.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: span() computes the wrong range with exact=True and open bounds - literally the inclusive/exclusive endpoint bug that breaks last_7_days and month_to_date.
A range check uses strict < where it must be <=, rejecting valid boundary values. The exact off-by-one class this task punishes.
Duration arithmetic over months and leap years produces wrong dates; calendar-aware date arithmetic, which month_to_date needs.
parse_date raises for year-only, ordinal and week date forms; robust parsing of date strings into real dates.
utcnow() returns local time instead of UTC - getting 'now' wrong shifts every relative window, exactly what a reference date guards against.
parse_date crashes on the YYYY-MM form because the missing day is not defaulted; partial-date handling in a date parser.
Parsing dates against an explicit format token string (YYYY-MMM-DD) is broken; format-driven date extraction, as from a filename pattern.
parse_iso fails outright on ISO datetime strings; date-string-to-object conversion in the same library family.
12-hour formatting returns 00 for 1 PM; a boundary-value error in date/time rendering.
humanize gives wrong values for minute/hour/year granularities; bucketing an elapsed interval into the right unit.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Select indices older than N units by parsing a date out of the index name with a timestring - parse-date-from-name plus relative window, the core of this task.
The 'period' filtertype (relative date ranges over dated artifacts) fails for snapshots; debugging relative-period date filtering end to end.
Pattern filter only matches at the start of the name instead of anywhere; filename-pattern matching over dated log artifacts.
A midnight schedule fires an hour late after DST starts; calendar-boundary arithmetic going subtly wrong, like a day boundary off by one.
groupby-resample-count returns an inconsistent type; counting records per time bucket, the same aggregation this task performs.
Log files rotate into the wrong file when the rotation time boundary is hit; assigning log records to the right dated file.
Timestamp conversion is wrong whenever the local timezone is not UTC; the classic reason a 'today' bucket silently shifts.
A timedelta cooloff window is not applied as expected; a rolling time window that must expire entries at the right moment.
Commit timestamp plus timezone offset blows up when the offset is out of range; converting a raw timestamp into a dated record.
ISO 8601 datetime parsing crashes on a now-nullable field; defensive parsing of date strings from external records.

final_top10.reason: Per-level INFO/WARN/ERROR counting over log files, with the specific trap of level words appearing inside message text.
Parse the date out of an artifact's name with a timestring and select those inside a relative age window. Both halves of this task.
Logs named app_<YYYY-MM-DD>.log carrying LEVEL records; date comes from the filename, selection from the level.
Time-bucketed log counts with zeros for empty buckets, written to summary.csv with an exact header and sort order.
Per-day counts over a full calendar month into a Date,Count CSV, including days with no events. Calendar-window aggregation.
The relative 'period' date-range filter works for one artifact type but not another; debugging relative-window selection logic.
An explicitly inclusive 30-day window anchored on a reference point, with per-day counts inside it.
Counts per day from 30 days ago through today, one day at a time; the inclusive rolling window plus a daily histogram in shell.
Wrong span endpoints with exact=True and open bounds - the inclusive/exclusive boundary bug that silently corrupts last_7_days.
Accept only the exact level tokens and skip everything else, then bucket by time and aggregate. Same strict-token plus windowing.

notes: This TB2.1 task is common in shape, so all five corpora had real candidates and the top 10 is genuinely spread across four of them. Two finds worth flagging for the merge: the elastic/curator cluster in SWE-Rebench (603, 1175, 1355) is the best non-TMax material in the whole pool for 'parse a date out of a name and filter by a relative window', and neither was in the shortlist; and SWE-Smith's arrow/isodate cluster is a dense source of inclusive-versus-exclusive boundary bugs, which is the single most likely way to fail this task. The RTS 'dokey 30-day sparkline' family is near-duplicated across many ids - I kept five because they differ in how they phrase the window (inclusive, 30-day, 31-day), which is exactly the distinction that matters, but a merge step should probably keep only one or two to avoid flooding the set with near-clones. Lexical retrieval over-weighted generic 'log analyst' ETL chores that never touch date windows.
